## Research

::: {.research-grid}
::: {.research-card}
<p class="eyebrow">Language model inference</p>

### Faster generation at matched performance

Methods for accelerating autoregressive and diffusion language models, including relaxed speculative decoding and Fréchet profile decoding.

[Read about this research](research.html#language-model-inference)
:::

::: {.research-card}
<p class="eyebrow">Classification and privacy</p>

### How modeling choices change behavior

Work on generative and discriminative classification, shortcut learning, concept shift, calibration, and membership inference attacks.

[Read about this research](research.html#classification-privacy)
:::

::: {.research-card}
<p class="eyebrow">Search and recommendation</p>

### Learning under sparse feedback

Production research on search relevance, multimodal calibration, long tail ranking, counterfactual analysis, and experimentation.

[Read about this research](research.html#search-recommendation)
:::

::: {.research-card}
<p class="eyebrow">Statistical learning</p>

### Dependence beyond correlation

Mixture models, copulas, high dimensional clustering, time series, and sequential decision making.

[Read about this research](research.html#statistical-learning)
:::
:::

::: {.math-window}
<p class="eyebrow">From the notebook</p>

For a differentiable transformation `g_θ` of noise `ε` whose distribution does not depend on `θ`, the pathwise gradient is

$$
\nabla_\theta
\mathbb{E}_{\varepsilon \sim p(\varepsilon)}
\left[f\!\left(g_\theta(\varepsilon)\right)\right]
=
\mathbb{E}_{\varepsilon \sim p(\varepsilon)}
\left[\nabla_\theta f\!\left(g_\theta(\varepsilon)\right)\right].
$$

[Read the note on reparameterization gradients](writing/reparameterization-gradients.html)
:::
